name: scan-progress
title: Scan Progress
description: An analysing state for media: a scan band lights pixel squares over the image while a ring fills a pill.

perf.budget: The pixel field is three Skia paths rebuilt 30 times a second by one worklet while scanning; it stops completely when done. The ring is one trimmed path.

measurements.notes: Animating while scanning: the pixel field redraws 30 times a second and the spinner turns; both stop when done. Most of each frame is the emulator GPU swap.

a11y.reducedMotion: No pixel field or spinner rotation; the wash, the ring and the labels still show progress.
a11y.screenReader: The pill is a progress bar named by the current step, with its percentage when known; changes are announced. Pass imageLabel to describe the image.

meta.guide:
## Usage

```tsx
import { ScanProgress } from '@/components/kinetik/scan-progress';

<ScanProgress
  source={{ uri: video.thumbnail }}
  imageLabel="Your swing, frame 1"
  progress={job.progress}
  done={job.status === 'complete'}
  label={job.stepLabel}
/>;
```

Leave out `progress` when the work has no measurable progress: the ring creeps towards 90% and slows down, and closes when `done` turns true.

## When to use

- Processing a photo or video the person just gave you: AI analysis, enhancement, background removal, upload checks.
- Waits of a few seconds to a minute, where seeing the image being worked on reassures.

## When not to use

- Instant results under a second: the effect would only flash.
- Waits without an image: use a progress bar or Ring Spinner.

## Notes

- `label` changes cross-fade, so you can name each step as it happens.
- The pixel field draws white squares over the image; pick a `tint` that suits your photos (it defaults to the theme success green).
- With reduced motion the pixel field and spinner rotation are left out; the ring and labels still report progress.

docs: Prefer `npx kinetik-ui add scan-progress`: it installs dependencies with expo install, so versions match your Expo SDK.
